overview: Typically, a bachelor’s degree takes about 3 years and a master’s degree about 1-2 years, depending on the institution.

Studying in Switzerland connects Indian students with world-leading technical institutes like ETH Zurich and EPFL, exceptionally low public semester fees, high living standards, and global innovation hubs.

Edu Hawk Worldwide Consultancy guides Indian students through Swiss cantonal application procedures, embassy document authentication, proof of funds requirements, and post-study opportunities across Europe.

sections.title: What is the duration of the Law course in Switzerland?
sections.lead: Typically, a bachelor’s degree takes about 3 years and a master’s degree about 1-2 years, depending on the institution.

sections.title: How much do you pay for studying law in Switzerland?
sections.lead: The estimated annual tuition and living expenses for students are around ₹12 lakh to ₹30 lakh or more depending on the university and city.

sections.title: Top Universities to Consider in Switzerland
sections.lead: Explore world-leading Swiss cantonal universities and federal institutes of technology offering globally renowned degrees, modern research labs, and international faculty.

sections.title: Is it possible for Indian students to study Law in Switzerland after Class 12?
sections.lead: Yes, provided that the university accepts Indian qualifications and there are no other academic or language requirements.

sections.title: Do I need IELTS for Law in Switzerland?
sections.lead: Not all the time. The requirements depend on the language of instruction of the program and the university’s admission policy.

sections.title: I have studied in Switzerland, can I practice law in India?
sections.lead: No, not by default. The foreign law qualifications and professional eligibility need to be examined under the applicable Indian rules.
